subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled: false` become a hard read/exec access boundary for that skill's files, or remain a prompt/eligibility toggle with a separate strict access-control surface?
rationale: The code change is security-sensitive and compatibility-sensitive because existing configurations may rely on `enabled:false` only for prompt visibility while generic filesystem and exec policies still allow host paths.

options.title: Make enabled:false a hard boundary
options.body: Treat disabled skills as denied roots across skill visibility, file tools, exec, sandbox materialization, Gateway/UI status, docs, and tests, with an explicit upgrade note for affected operators.

options.title: Add a separate strict access policy
options.body: Preserve current `enabled:false` visibility semantics and introduce a new operator-controlled hard-deny or allowlist policy for skill files and execution.

options.title: Keep visibility-only semantics
options.body: Document that disabled skills only affect eligibility and require operators to use workspace, sandbox, and exec policy controls for isolation.

recommendation.title: Make enabled:false a hard boundary
recommendation.body: Treat disabled skills as denied roots across skill visibility, file tools, exec, sandbox materialization, Gateway/UI status, docs, and tests, with an explicit upgrade note for affected operators.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history and related skill/config work make this the strongest routing candidate for the security/config semantics decision.
